en: A proposed bill becomes a national law only after both the Senate and House of Representatives approve it and the President signs it.
The carabao plows muddy rice fields because its wide, cloven hooves prevent it from sinking deep into the soft soil.
The Philippine government declares a regular holiday by passing a specific law, which legally mandates paid time off for all workers on that designated date.
T'boli weavers create T'nalak cloth by tying and dyeing abaca fibers before weaving them into patterns inspired by their dreams.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator that uses hot water bottles to maintain a warm temperature for premature babies without electricity.
Devotees dance the Sinulog festival's two-steps-forward, one-step-backward movement to mimic the rhythmic flow of the river, honoring the Santo Niño.
Filipino citizens exercise their right to vote by registering with the COMELEC and casting secret ballots to elect their public officials.
Jose Rizal wrote Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish friar abuses, which ultimately awakened Filipino nationalism and sparked the revolution.
The ancient Baybayin writing system represents syllables rather than single letters, requiring a small mark to change a basic vowel sound into a consonant-vowel pair.
The Sampaguita flower releases its strongest fragrance at night because its white petals open fully in the dark to attract nocturnal pollinating moths.
The Barangay Captain resolves local community disputes by convening the Lupong Tagapamayapa, which facilitates mediation before conflicts escalate to formal courts.
In the traditional Bayanihan practice, neighbors physically lift a nipa hut's bamboo frame onto their shoulders to relocate the entire house for a family.
